clue.text: US agent skirting shaft dropped litter

indicators.note: skirting means running round the edge of, so the agent's letters go either side of the shaft

parts.note: a fed is an informal American name for an FBI agent
an arrow is a shaft fired from a bow

explanation.surface: An American agent sidesteps a lift shaft and drops some rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' looks like rubbish dropped on the street; here it is a brood of piglets.
explanation.definitionFit: A sow that has given birth to a brood of piglets is said to have farrowed.

clue.text: Singular sound of cat getting bird

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
a mew is the cry a cat makes

explanation.surface: A lone cat yowls as it catches a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The smew is a small diving duck of northern Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Abruptly stop talk of ransoms

indicators.note: talk of means the word is as it would be spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: to ransom a captive is to pay to free them, so ransoms means frees

explanation.surface: Someone abruptly halts the discussion of kidnap payments.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt suddenly and stay motionless is to go rigid in place, as a startled animal does.

clue.text: Resolution almost lost in course of recovery

indicators.note: in means the shortened word sits within the course of recovery

parts.note: a cure is a course of treatment that brings recovery

indicators.note: almost means the word lost loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A patient's determination nearly vanished during their convalescence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolution' looks like determination; here it is the sense of a matter being settled. 'almost' drops the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Closure is the sense of an ending or settlement reached, as when a matter is finally put to rest.

clue.text: Strikers in this game come to blows

parts.note: a match is a game between two sides
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Footballers' tempers flare and a game turns into a punch-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikers' looks like forwards on a football pitch; here they are matches, struck to light, which sit in this container.
explanation.definitionFit: Matches are struck to light them, and the small cardboard container keeps them together.

clue.text: Bachelor scans second item from bakery

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees
to scan a text is to read it
a tick is an informal word for a moment or second

explanation.surface: A single man reads through a list and picks out a second loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A long thin crisp stick of baked dough is sold by bakers, often served with dips.

clue.text: Wanting courage primarily to stop fright

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so the letter goes inside the fright

parts.note: a scare is a sudden fright

indicators.note: primarily means the opening letter of the word courage

explanation.surface: Someone lacking nerve tries to summon courage to stop being afraid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in short supply is lacking or wanting, as in 'food was wanting'.

clue.text: Leading lady's retreat just after party goes west

indicators.note: after means the word for just follows the party
in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, so the party is backwards

parts.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the UK Labour Party
moral means just or righteous

explanation.surface: A first lady retreats just after a party collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading lady' is the monarch, not an actress; BALMORAL is the British royal family's castle in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal estate in Aberdeenshire is where the British monarch traditionally spends summer holidays.

clue.text: Here Livingstone found father in main road, car being tailed

indicators.note: in means father sits inside the main road

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, London to Edinburgh, written AI
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: being tailed means the car has its tail, its last letter, cut off

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: Livingstone's father is found in a main road with a car being followed.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh, with the 1 read as I. David Livingstone was the Scottish explorer famously 'found' by Stanley.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian explorer and missionary spent his career exploring the continent's interior, where Stanley tracked him down.

clue.text: Develop grand argument

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds
a row is a noisy argument

explanation.surface: A major quarrel starts to develop.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop is to mature or increase in size, as a seedling does.

clue.text: Child introduced to light music, part of suite?

indicators.note: introduced to means the child abbreviation is put inside the music

parts.note: easy airs are undemanding tunes

explanation.surface: A child gets a taste of light classical music, perhaps a movement from a suite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suite' looks like a musical suite next to 'music'; it is a three-piece suite of furniture, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-piece suite is a sofa plus two matching armchairs, so these comfy seats belong to one.

clue.text: Sew unlined articles together to form bandage

indicators.note: unlined means with the inside, the lining, removed, leaving the outer letters of Sew

parts.note: a and the are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: A tailor stitches unlined pieces into a dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap something in strips of cloth, as with a dressing, is to swaddle or bind it.

clue.text: It's a little naughty and teases

indicators.note: naughty suggests misbehaviour, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something slightly risqué arouses and teases.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface describes a mildly racy tease, which is what the answer does.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite someone pleasurably, often by a hint of the risqué, is to tantalise or tease them.

clue.text: Routers created with British investment less likely to break down

indicators.note: investment means clothing or putting inside, so British goes within
created suggests making something new, so the letters of Routers are rearranged

explanation.surface: Network routers built with British money should be more reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'created' turns ROUTERS into ROUSTER, and 'with investment' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardier, sturdier equipment is tougher and so less prone to failure.

clue.text: Our bosses reviewed corruption within faction

indicators.note: reviewed is read as re-viewed, looked at the other way, so the whole is reversed
within means corruption goes inside the faction

parts.note: a side is a faction or team
rot is decay or corruption

explanation.surface: Our managers have looked into corruption inside a political faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our' fits because the setter writes for a newspaper, whose content is run by these bosses; 'reviewed' reverses the whole SROTIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper crosswords are commissioned and overseen by the paper's senior journalists in charge of content.

clue.text: Consider acquiring inverted nose ring

indicators.note: acquiring means the word for consider takes the other letters inside

parts.note: to rate something is to consider or regard it

indicators.note: inverted means the word nose is turned upside down, read backwards in a down clue

explanation.surface: Someone considers getting an upside-down nose ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like jewellery next to 'nose', but it is a verb meaning to sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell that rings echoes and reverberates, filling the space with sound.

clue.text: Former hamper missing in display

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: missing means the word in is taken away from the synonym for hamper

parts.note: to inhibit is to hamper or restrain

explanation.surface: A picnic hamper that used to be on show has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes IN off INHIBIT to leave HIBIT. 'hamper' looks like a basket but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An item shown publicly in a gallery or museum is a showpiece or exhibit.

clue.text: Where unionised actors met prejudice?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, the place is within the British actors' trade union, called Equity
prejudice causes unfairness and injustice; the question mark flags the loose fit

explanation.definitionFit: Unfair treatment and injustice are the results of bias, so the word stands loosely for prejudice.

clue.text: Old Indian currency note turned up, praise be

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the anna was a former Indian coin, a sixteenth of a rupee
soh is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Praise be: an old Indian coin and banknote have turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry of adoration in Christian and Jewish worship is an exclamation glorifying God.

clue.text: Galilean satellite first penetrating rings

indicators.note: penetrating means first goes inside the letters for rings

parts.note: rings gives CALL (a phone call is a ring) and O (a letter shaped like a ring)
1st, written IST, is the short form of first

explanation.surface: Galileo's moon was the first to pass through the rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Galilean' looks like it means from Galilee; it refers to Galileo, who discovered Jupiter's four largest moons.
explanation.definitionFit: Jupiter's four big moons were discovered by Galileo in 1610 and this is one of them.

clue.text: Ultimate height of a river that amazes me

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
gee is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: The highest point of a river is something that amazes me.
explanation.definitionFit: The apogee is the highest point of an orbit or the peak of a career, a climax.

clue.text: Length initially taken off decorative chain

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged
initially means the opening letter of the word Length

explanation.surface: A long decorative chain was cut short and removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet-like chain worn round the lower leg above the foot is an item of jewellery.

clue.text: Exact payment for archdeacon to get old clothes

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the word for old dresses, wraps round, the archdeacon

parts.note: age means to grow old
Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: An archdeacon demands payment to receive some old clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' looks like garments; here it is a verb meaning wraps round.
explanation.definitionFit: To take revenge for a wrong is to exact retribution or payment for it.

clue.text: Foremost dons moaned about contribution to online address

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the rearranged letters wear the other word inside them
about means the letters of moaned are rearranged

parts.note: main means chief or foremost

explanation.surface: Senior university fellows grumbled about adding to the web address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university teachers; it is a verb meaning puts on. 'about' makes DONAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A web URL includes the registered identifier of a site, such as guardian.co.uk.

clue.text: Sporting contest, though there's nothing in it

indicators.note: in it means nothing sits inside the word for though

parts.note: but means though or however
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A sporting contest, though nothing came of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's nothing in it' sounds like a close contest; it is the instruction to put O inside BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing or wrestling match is called a bout.

clue.text: Root crop and pulse picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as by a microphone, so a word of the same sound is used

parts.note: a beat is a pulse or rhythmic throb

explanation.surface: A farmer harvests root vegetables and pulses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' looks like a crop of peas or beans next to 'Root crop'; it is a heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar beet and beetroot are grown for their swollen edible roots.

clue.text: Colonel's first to board plane, after troops decline

indicators.note: after means the plane comes following the troops

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army troops

indicators.note: to board a plane is to get on it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a jet is a plane

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word Colonel's

explanation.surface: The colonel boards the plane first, after the troops refuse to go.
explanation.definitionFit: To refuse an offer is to turn it down or decline it.

clue.text: Doesn't care for rebellious general Celts butchered

indicators.note: rebellious suggests turning against, so the abbreviation is reversed
butchered means hacked about, so the letters of Celts are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rebel general slaughtered the Celts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebellious' gives NEG and 'butchered' gives LECTS; the definition is a verb phrase, not about caring for people.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail to look after someone or something is to leave it uncared for.
